accepted_scope_caveats.label: Open-ended Question 1 / ass:nondegenerate-oracle-risk
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The feasible-inference target is conditional on the stated moment, maximum-unit, and nondegenerate oracle-risk triangular-array regime; these regularity conditions are not claimed to be derived.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The question asks for oracle-risk equivalence and studentized coverage only uniformly over finite populations satisfying those stated conditions with fixed T, r, and L.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies GLS estimation of instantaneous and lagged effects under Specification (3.1), and Theorem 3.1 gives optimality conditions for a five-stage S-shaped treated-fraction design.
The paper uses Lagrange polynomial interpolation for staggered-rollout estimators of the total treatment effect under a degree-bounded network-interference potential-outcome model.

The paper defines finite-population dynamic causal effects for panel experiments, derives limiting distributions through its sequential-assignment framework, and provides conservative and exact randomization inference procedures.

The preprint studies staggered rollout cluster randomized experiments with randomized adoption times and establishes finite-population consistency, asymptotic normality, and conservative variance estimation for regression estimators.
The paper derives an efficient estimator in a staggered-treatment-timing linear class and an asymptotically unbiased feasible plug-in estimator with weakly dominating efficiency.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add a short boundary corollary formally showing that every T greater than or equal to the frontier remains feasible, with an explicit extension of the canonical schedule and representer.
Add a quantified misspecification corollary for an omitted degree-(r+1) secular component, expressing resulting sustained-effect bias through the terminal finite-difference functional.
Turn the inference handle into a concrete cross-fitted covariance learner and prove a unit-cluster Hájek linearization and studentized finite-population limit law under primitive conditions.

recommended_next_step: Advance to Stage 0 to prove the sharp-stage frontier and its two target-active deficit aliases; retain feasible studentization as the separately conditional open inference rung.
